title: Marseille sporting director Medhi Benatia to remain at club – two days after resigning
content:
Marseille’s American owner Frank McCourt has confirmed Medhi Benatia will remain in his role until the end of the season — just two days after the sporting director resigned.

In the latest twist, McCourt revealed that Benatia had agreed to stay through until the end of June and will head up all sporting activities.

That comes just two days after Benatia announced on his social media channels that he had submitted his resignation, citing “tensions surrounding the leadership”.

He added how he felt “a growing dissatisfaction, a rift that I deeply regret…in Marseille, results are the only judge”.

Benatia’s announcement on Sunday came after head coach Roberto De Zerbi left Marseille, with the club confirming that news at 2.35am on Wednesday morning local time.

De Zerbi left by mutual consent following a dramatic fortnight that saw Marseille eliminated from the Champions League at the group stage and then humiliated 5-0 by Paris Saint-Germain in Le Classique.

In the wake of De Zerbi’s exit, Benatia told L’Equipe: “When a coach leaves, it’s like a member of the family is leaving. It always hurts. He is far from being the only one at fault. We will have to find better solutions.”

De Zerbi’s exit didn’t spell the end of the drama, however.

In Marseille’s following match, at home to Strasbourg on February 14, there were protests in the stands, while Marseille threw away a 2-0 lead to draw 2-2 with Gary O’Neil’s side scoring a 96th-minute equaliser.

That result leaves Marseille five points behind a resurgent Lyon, who have won 13 matches in a row, in third. The top three in France qualify automatically for next season’s Champions League.

They are still in the Coupe de France, where they face Toulouse in a quarter-final game at the Velodrome on March 4.

Elsewhere in a statement released on Tuesday, McCourt said chairman Pablo Longoria’s remit will move towards his “institutional responsibilities, in order to maintain the representation of Olympique de Marseille within French and particularly European bodies”.

McCourt said: “As the owner of the club, I am coming to Marseille and once again taking on my responsibilities so that the club remains focused on its objectives, particularly qualification for the next Champions League and a strong run in the Coupe de France.

“Under the supervision of Mehdi Benatia, the appointment of a new coach will be announced shortly. My ambition for the club remains intact. Let us mobilise in the service of OM.”

Marseille have still not communicated about the latest news on their official club channels.
